title: Bind ToolRole to the WriteLease. dispatch must read the role from the lease, never from the role string the caller passes. A tool the granted role does not hold is refused with a named rule stating the role that would allow it.

Enforce phase on dispatch. A tool not legal in the session current phase is refused with a named rule stating the current phase, what is available in it, and how to promote. Verified today: unwrap_uvs (POLISH) and add_railing (REFINE) both succeeded while phase was blockout.

Real OS-concurrency tests on the write lock: genuine threads contending for acquire, a second writer refused while a lease is live, INSPECT readers running concurrently with a writer, lease expiry under contention, dead-writer recovery. Zero threading.Thread exists anywhere in the lock test surface today. This is the property the whole design assumes and the thing the pass is judged on.

can_promote evaluates real per-phase AcceptanceQuery objects against live geometry via measure.evaluate. Remove the force=True override. Every failing query names the object, the measured value, the threshold missed, and the operation that would fix it — that message is load-bearing, not cosmetic, because there is no override behind it.

export_scene and check_export_budget get real ToolSpec.handler callables invoked directly by dispatch, outside the operation log. Remove the carve-out at app/app_test.py:66 so the every-registered-tool-is-executable assertion becomes total.

Publish MEASURE_SPECS: distance, gap_width, angle, find_clipping, full defect report. Assigned to the INSPECT role, which has zero tools today. This is the product central claim and the largest gap against blender-ai-mcp.
Add inspect and promote tools: get_phase, list_objects, describe_object, promote_phase. Without these an agent cannot see what it built, learn what phase it is in, advance, or finish.
Publish DETAIL_SPECS for the three detail passes named first-class at Gate A 8.4 and currently holding zero tools.

forge3d serve starts viewer.serve() automatically alongside the MCP transport. Today the socket is never opened, so no browser can reach a running session and the entire built control surface is unreachable.

Undo: reject at apply() an operation targeting an object no logged operation produced, with a named rule; AND make replay() tolerant of a single operation that cannot re-run, skipping and reporting rather than aborting. Today one such operation makes undo/redo/rollback raise for the rest of the session.

undo/redo/rollback_to restore from barrier.snapshot_path when an undo barrier is crossed, instead of replaying the opaque operation. Verified today: a non-deterministic raw script produced 1 object, then 3 differently-named objects after undo+redo, while reporting FULL_RESYNC. The capture half already exists.

Scene document v2: serialise placements, joinery, acceptance, asset_class and proposal_id. SCHEMA_VERSION to 2. A v1 file loads with an explicit named warning that its constraints were never stored. Round-trip test per nested type.

Every failure names a rule. Broad catch at the app/handlers.py boundary mapping any unhandled exception to a real rule carrying the original detail, PLUS degeneracy checks (zero-length path, zero quaternion, empty point set) moved into validate_params so good cases never reach the floor.

The automatic post-operation check runs pairwise find_clipping and find_visual_gaps against spatial neighbours, matching the checks_scope: "changed+neighbours" it already reports. One small room produced 39 unreported clipping defects; sweeping 480 pairs by hand took 14ms.

find_self_intersections uses the spatial index for broadphase pruning. Today it is an O(triangles^2) pure-Python sweep: 0.006s to create a 960-triangle sphere, 6.5s to check it and find nothing — about 40% of a realistic session. F-014 adds load to the same loop.
Verify 1 Roblox stud = 0.28 m against Roblox own documentation, cite the source in export_profiles.py, and pin it with a regression test. Currently an uncited guess in the primary export profile.

Summarise the post-operation report above a threshold: per-object detail while it is a handful, aggregate plus breakdown plus defects beyond that. add_railing currently returns ~3,398 tokens for 40 objects; a small room costs ~5,400.
Tune bevel parameters and add a topology cleanup pass. Real Blender bevels currently give mean triangle aspect ratio ~116 and edge-length CoV ~1.6 on a simple tread. Closes B-00L.

Measure the object-creation and check-loop curve to a real few thousand objects, not ~900. Record where it bends, and what the viewer and the check loop cost at that size. Gate A 11.4 named thousands as the target.

Install Puppeteer and add a smoke test: the page loads against a live backend, the canvas draws, the action log updates. Not the full interaction and layout suite (cut at Gate B 6.1). Nothing has ever run this frontend in a browser.

add_railing reports the cross-sections it supplied when the agent omitted post_size/baluster_size/rail_size, so the 5cm/5cm/3cm defaults stop being invisible. Gate A 6.4 chose no built-in dimension table.
Delete _tool_registry.py and its tests; Orchestrator.tools_for delegates to the real mcp_server registry. Its 16 tool names match none of the 29 real ones and nothing in src/app calls it.
Delete create_engine(prefer_subprocess=True) and correct docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:34,43, which still describes the subprocess fallback as a working part of the engine surface.

Record actual per-role tool counts after F-005..F-008 land, and state plainly where a role exceeds the 5-8 accuracy-optimal band. Gate B 3.3 chose to exceed it deliberately and measure rather than split roles.

Add the missing spacing <= 0 guard to engine/_curve.py sample_polyline, which loops forever if called directly; its twin in testing/mesh_helpers.py:51 already has it. Reconcile the four _triangle_normal copies on their degenerate-case return value (three return None, constraints/anchors.py returns Vec3 zero and re-checks 1e-9 rather than EPSILON at :95).

Correct the four stale module docs: mcp_server/CLAUDE.md and README.md describe the package collision as live and blocking when it is fixed and claim the SDK is not installed when it is; viewer/CLAUDE.md says the same of websockets/starlette; orchestration/README.md still frames src/scene as unbuilt.

Add the one required justification line to the seven files marginally over the 300-line soft cap (contracts_test.py 530, operations.py 408, fake_engine.py 392, geometry.py 345, measurement.py 325, engine.py 319, app/handlers.py 310). Five are in contracts/ where splitting is explicitly disfavoured.
Set status "done" on the 24 backlog entries (B-001..B-021, B-023..B-025, B-027) that are built and green but carry no status field, in the archived .pipeline/backlog-pass-1.json.
